def expensive_items(dataset, n):
    """
    Returns the list of n most expensive items from the dataset.
    
    Args:
        dataset (list[dict]): A list of dictionaries containing 'name' and 'price'.
        n (int): The number of top-expensive items to return.
        
    Returns:
        list[dict]: List of the n most expensive item dictionaries.
    """
    # Sort by price in descending order (-x['price'] ensures reverse sort)
    sorted_items = sorted(dataset, key=lambda x: -x['price'])
    
    # Slice to get only the top n items
    return sorted_items[:n]

# Test case based on your assertion
result = expensive_items([{'name': 'Item-1', 'price': 101.1}, {'name': 'Item-2', 'price': 555.22}], 1)
print(result) 
# Expected Output: [{'name': 'Item-2', 'price': 555.22}]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert expensive_items([{'name': 'Item-1', 'price': 101.1}, {'name': 'Item-2', 'price': 555.22}], 1) == [{'name': 'Item-2', 'price': 555.22}]
print("Assertion passed!")
